correctness.rationale: Direct evaluation of the weight-zero Rota-Baxter identity on all four ordered basis pairs yields the polynomial system a^2-2ad=0, ab=0, b^2=0, bd=0. Over a field b^2=0 forces b=0, leaving exactly a(a-2d)=0. The automorphism group follows from multiplicativity of the image of e1, and direct conjugation gives the stated affine action on c. The normal forms and finite-field counts then follow by explicit orbit analysis. A standalone symbolic and finite-field checker reconstructs all equations and reproduces the q=2,3,5,7 counts.

value.rationale: The 2018 literature already treats the raw operator family as part of a complete low-dimensional classification, so quotienting it by the full automorphism group is the natural moduli refinement. The result is not merely a normalization: characteristic two collapses an entire set-theoretic component and changes both the operator count and the conjugacy-class count. The exact finite-field formulas provide a reusable boundary case for low-dimensional Rota-Baxter Leibniz moduli across characteristics.
